# Compliance framework and accountability

How this baseline implements **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A**, **NIS2 (Directive 2022/2555,
art. 21(2))**, **CIS Controls v8.1** and **NIST CSF 2.0** — and what the organisation has to arrange
itself on top of that. Intended for a CISO, DPO or auditor. Everything below is derived from the
`controls` field in [`IntuneTemplate/_manifest.json`](../IntuneTemplate/_manifest.json) and the vocabulary in
[`IntuneTemplate/_controls.json`](../IntuneTemplate/_controls.json).

**Read this first.** This document states what the *baseline* enforces, not what a *tenant* does. Whether
the policies are present and applied in a tenant is evidenced through Intune reporting: the
assignment and the per-device status of every policy named below.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| ● Covered (phase 1) | at least one policy in phase 1 enforces or verifies the measure |
| ◐ Pilot, waiting or dedicated group only | the policy exists, but is in phase 2, 3 or 4: not yet on all devices |
| ▢ Organisational | cannot be implemented with endpoint or identity policy: process, people, physical or another technical domain |
| ○ No technical measure in the baseline | can be implemented technically, but this baseline does not (or only with an alternative in phase 5) |

> **Conditional Access is deliberately not included** (`--no-ca`). MFA (NIS2 (j)) and access conditions rely largely on CA; the accountability for that is in the CA repo.

## ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A

Standard: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A — NEN-EN-ISO/IEC 27001:2023 (+A1:2024 does not change Annex A). The titles are the official English titles. **Implementable** states whether the
control can be implemented with endpoint or identity policy; **Status** states what this baseline does with it today.

### 5 Organizational controls

| Control | Implementable | Status | Phase 1 | Other | What remains needed organisationally |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| **A.5.1** Policies for information security | organisational | ▢ Organisational | – | – | Define the information security policy and topic-specific policies (including endpoint, access and AI policies), have them approved by management and review them periodically. |
| **A.5.2** Information security roles and responsibilities | organisational | ▢ Organisational | – | – | Appoint and document the baseline owner, CISO and administrative roles (Intune, Entra and Defender administration). |
| **A.5.3** Segregation of duties | partial | ○ No technical measure in the baseline | – | – | Separation between who changes policies, who approves them (PR review) and who grants exceptions; set up Entra/Intune RBAC and PIM — outside the scope of this baseline. |
| **A.5.4** Management responsibilities | organisational | ▢ Organisational | – | – | Management demonstrably drives compliance (NIS2 art. 20: management bodies approve the measures and follow training). |
| **A.5.5** Contact with authorities | organisational | ▢ Organisational | – | – | Document points of contact with the CSIRT/NCSC, the supervisory authority and the data protection authority (AP), including reporting deadlines. |
| **A.5.6** Contact with special interest groups | organisational | ▢ Organisational | – | – | Organise participation in ISACs, sector consultations and supplier advisories. |
| **A.5.7** Threat intelligence | partial | ○ No technical measure in the baseline | – | – | Have threat intelligence (Defender, Entra ID Protection, NCSC) assessed and translated into adjustments to the baseline. |
| **A.5.8** Information security in project management | organisational | ▢ Organisational | – | – | Include security requirements in projects, for example when rolling out new devices or platforms. |

| [**A.5.10** Acceptable use of information and other associated assets](#a510-acceptable-use-of-information-and-other-associated-assets) | partial | ● Covered (phase 1) | 3 | 11 | Define and communicate rules of use (including AI and private use); technology enforces only part of them. |
| **A.5.11** Return of assets | partial | ○ No technical measure in the baseline | – | – | Offboarding process: returning devices, retire/wipe in Intune, blocking the account. |

| **A.5.13** Labelling of information | organisational | ▢ Organisational | – | – | Labelling procedure and tools (Purview sensitivity labels) — outside the scope of this baseline. |

Microsoft, AI services, remote support tools); technology can only block unapproved services. |

## NIS2 art. 21(2)

Source: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2), art. 21(2); elaborated in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690, Annex. Per point: what the baseline does technically, which policies those are,
how it can be evidenced, and what the organisation has to arrange itself. Article 21 requires measures that are
*appropriate and proportionate* based on a risk analysis; this baseline is a reasoned implementation
of the technical part, not a replacement for that assessment.

### art. 21(2)(a) policies on risk analysis and information system security

*Policies on risk analysis and information system security* — elaborated in Annex §1–2 of the implementing regulation.

**Technical implementation.** This baseline is an elaboration of the security policy for devices and access, but not a risk analysis.

**Intune, phase 1 (0)**

- none

**Evidence route.** No technical measure in phase 1, so no technical evidence route either.

**Needed organisationally**

- Risk analysis (for example a BIA and risk register) that substantiates the choice of measures
- Network and information security policy, approved by the management body (art. 20)
- Periodic review of policy and risk analysis
- Register of accepted residual risks and organisational decisions (see Organisational decisions in this document)

### art. 21(2)(b) incident handling

*Incident handling* — elaborated in Annex §3 of the implementing regulation.

**Technical implementation.** EDR onboarding, audit logging, PowerShell logging and the risk-based CA policies provide detection and the means to intervene.

**Intune, phase 1 (8)**

- [`MAC - D - Defender for Endpoint`](../IntuneTemplate/MAC/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_MAC_D_Defender_for_Endpoint.en.md) (phase 1)
- [`MAC - D - Time Server`](../IntuneTemplate/MAC/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_MAC_D_Time_Server.en.md) (phase 1)
- [`WIN - D - Audit and Event Logging`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Audit_and_Event_Logging.en.md) (phase 1)
- [`WIN - D - Audit Policy Enforcement`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Audit_Policy_Enforcement.en.md) (phase 1)
- [`WIN - D - Defender EDR Policy`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Defender_EDR_Policy.en.md) (phase 1)
- [`WIN - D - Logging`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Logging.en.md) (phase 1)
- [`WIN - D - Security Hardening`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Security_Hardening.en.md) (phase 1)
- [`WIN - D - Timezone`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Timezone.en.md) (phase 1)

**Prepared — pilot, waiting or dedicated group (6)**

- [`WIN - D - Security Log Monitoring`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Security_Log_Monitoring.en.md) (phase 2)
- [`AND - U - Compliance Corporate Defender for Endpoint`](../IntuneTemplate/AND/CompliancePolicies/Baseline_AND_U_Compliance_Corporate_Defender_for_Endpoint.en.md) (phase 3)
- [`AND - U - Compliance Defender for Endpoint`](../IntuneTemplate/AND/CompliancePolicies/Baseline_AND_U_Compliance_Defender_for_Endpoint.en.md) (phase 3)
- [`IOS - U - Compliance Defender for Endpoint`](../IntuneTemplate/IOS/CompliancePolicies/Baseline_IOS_U_Compliance_Defender_for_Endpoint.en.md) (phase 3)
- [`WIN - D - Windows Event Forwarding`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Windows_Event_Forwarding.en.md) (phase 3)
- [`WIN - U - Compliance Defender for Endpoint Risk`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/CompliancePolicies/Baseline_WIN_U_Compliance_Defender_for_Endpoint_Risk.en.md) (phase 3)

**Alternative, not deployed (1)**: `WIN - D - Defender for Endpoint EDR`

**Evidence route.** Intune reporting: the assignment and the per-device status of the policies above.

**Needed organisationally**

- Incident response plan with roles and playbooks
- Notification procedure to the CSIRT/supervisory authority within 24 hours (early warning), 72 hours and 1 month (art. 23)
- Follow-up of alerts (who watches when, escalation)
- Central log storage and retention periods
- Post-incident review

### art. 21(2)(c) business continuity and crisis management

*Business continuity, such as backup management and disaster recovery, and crisis management* — elaborated in Annex §4 of the implementing regulation.

**Technical implementation.** OneDrive Known Folder Move, Windows backup, Quick Machine Recovery and a fallback network contribute; they do not replace a backup of M365 data.

**Intune, phase 1 (7)**

### art. 21(2)(j) multi-factor authentication and secured communications

*The use of multi-factor authentication or continuous authentication solutions, secured voice, video and text communications and secured emergency communication systems* — elaborated in Annex §11.7 of the implementing regulation.

**Technical implementation.** Intune provides the strong authentication methods (Windows Hello for Business, passwordless sign-in); enforcing MFA happens in Conditional Access.

## NIST CSF 2.0

is organisational by definition: no policy implements it, this baseline is at most an execution of it.

## Organisational decisions and residual risks

What needs a management decision before the baseline is complete. Every row comes from `faseWaarom`
in the manifest; a decision here is a change of the phase in a PR, so that the decision and the
deployment can be found in one place.

### A. Choose a variant — phase 5, do not deploy (15)

Alternatives to a policy that is deployed, or organisational decisions without a technically correct answer. Assigning two
variants at the same time produces a Conflict in Intune, after which neither is applied.

| Policy | Why not deployed · related | Standards (ISO) |
|---|---|---|
| [`IOS - D - Apple Intelligence Permitted`](../IntuneTemplate/IOS/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_IOS_D_Apple_Intelligence_Permitted.en.md) | Alternative to the Restricted variant, for an organisation that permits Apple Intelligence on corporate devices. Assign one of them, never both. Related: `IOS - D - Apple Intelligence Restricted`. | A.5.10, A.5.34, A.8.12 |
| [`MAC - D - Apple Intelligence Permitted`](../IntuneTemplate/MAC/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_MAC_D_Apple_Intelligence_Permitted.en.md) | Alternative to the Restricted variant, for an organisation that permits Apple Intelligence in the workplace. Assign one of them, never both. Related: `MAC - D - Restrictions`, `MAC - D - Apple Intelligence Restricted`. | A.5.10, A.5.34, A.8.1 |
| [`MAC - D - External Storage Read Only`](../IntuneTemplate/MAC/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_MAC_D_External_Storage_Read_Only.en.md) | Organisational decision. Parity with [Baseline] - WIN - D - Removable Storage (phase 2, write blocked, read allowed) cannot be achieved on macOS: with ReadOnly, macOS does not fall back to mounting read-write media as read-only — Apple: 'external storage that is read-write will not be mounted read-only'. In practice this therefore blocks virtually all USB sticks and external drives, including for reading. That is a different decision than on Windows, and therefore not phase 2. Related: `WIN - D - Removable Storage`. | A.7.10, A.8.12 |
| [`WIN - D - Defender AV Policy`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Defender_AV_Policy.en.md) | The CIPP standard template alongside the OIB version, looser on three points. The OIB version is stricter — this one belongs nowhere. Related: `WIN - D - Defender Antivirus`. | A.8.7 |
| [`WIN - D - Defender for Endpoint EDR`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Defender_for_Endpoint_EDR.en.md) | Duplicates [Baseline] - WIN - D - Defender EDR Policy, which is deployed: assigning both puts two EDR policies on the same device. Until September 2026 this template carried the encrypted onboarding token of the tenant it was exported from; that has been replaced by the connector value, so the repo no longer contains a tenant-specific value. Related: `WIN - D - Defender EDR Policy`. | A.8.7, A.8.16 |
| [`WIN - D - Microsoft Edge DNS over HTTPS Secure`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Microsoft_Edge_DNS_over_HTTPS_Secure.en.md) | Alternative to the Automatic variant, only for an organisation with its own or contracted DoH resolver (for example a DNS filtering service) that can resolve internal names. Requires a tenant-specific resolver URL. Related: `WIN - D - Microsoft Edge DNS over HTTPS Automatic`. | A.8.20, A.8.24 |
| [`WIN - D - Microsoft Edge Search Engine`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/AdministrativeTemplates/Baseline_WIN_D_Microsoft_Edge_Search_Engine.en.md) | An organisational decision, not a security setting: which search engine is the default does not belong in a generic baseline. Only assign it if the organisation has decided so. | A.8.9 |
| [`WIN - D - Windows AI Features Permitted`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Windows_AI_Features_Permitted.en.md) | Alternative to the Restricted variant, for an organisation that permits generative AI in the workplace. Assign one of them, never both. Related: `WIN - D - Windows AI Features Restricted`, `WIN - D - Windows AI Restricted`, `WIN - U - AI Usage Control Restricted`. | A.5.10, A.5.34, A.8.1 |
| [`WIN - D - Windows AI Permitted`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Windows_AI_Permitted.en.md) | Alternative to the Restricted variant, for an organisation that permits Recall and Click To Do. Assign one of them, never both. Related: `WIN - D - Windows AI Restricted`. | A.5.10, A.5.34, A.8.1 |
| [`WIN - D - Windows Hello Passkey PIN Complexity Numeric`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Windows_Hello_Passkey_PIN_Complexity_Numeric.en.md) | Alternative to the alphanumeric variant, for an organisation that does not want to bear the helpdesk cost of a complex PIN. There are four PIN complexity policies and only one may ever be assigned: `WIN - D - Windows Hello Passkey PIN Complexity Alphanumeric` / `Numeric` (the passkey-named set) and `WIN - D - Windows Hello PIN Complexity Alphanumeric` / `Numeric` (the generic, older set). Two assigned policies that set the same setting to a different value produce a Conflict in Intune, after which neither is applied. | A.5.17, A.8.5 |
| [`WIN - D - Windows Hello PIN Complexity Alphanumeric`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Windows_Hello_PIN_Complexity_Alphanumeric.en.md) | Generically named predecessor of `WIN - D - Windows Hello Passkey PIN Complexity Alphanumeric`, which took over the deployment because its name says what it is about. Identical in content — the same four settings at the same values — so there is no reason to assign it. There are four PIN complexity policies and only one may ever be assigned: `WIN - D - Windows Hello Passkey PIN Complexity Alphanumeric` / `Numeric` (the passkey-named set) and `WIN - D - Windows Hello PIN Complexity Alphanumeric` / `Numeric` (the generic, older set). Two assigned policies that set the same setting to a different value produce a Conflict in Intune, after which neither is applied. | A.5.17, A.8.5 |
| [`WIN - D - Windows Hello PIN Complexity Numeric`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Windows_Hello_PIN_Complexity_Numeric.en.md) | Generically named predecessor of `WIN - D - Windows Hello Passkey PIN Complexity Numeric`. Alternative to the alphanumeric variant, for an organisation that does not want to bear the helpdesk cost of a complex PIN. There are four PIN complexity policies and only one may ever be assigned: `WIN - D - Windows Hello Passkey PIN Complexity Alphanumeric` / `Numeric` (the passkey-named set) and `WIN - D - Windows Hello PIN Complexity Alphanumeric` / `Numeric` (the generic, older set). Two assigned policies that set the same setting to a different value produce a Conflict in Intune, after which neither is applied. | A.5.17, A.8.5 |
| [`WIN - U - AI Usage Control Permitted`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_U_AI_Usage_Control_Permitted.en.md) | Alternative to the Restricted variant, for an organisation that permits public AI services. Assign one of them, never both. Related: `WIN - U - AI Usage Control Restricted`. | A.5.10, A.5.19, A.8.1, A.8.23 |
| [`WIN - U - Microsoft Outlook Cached Mode Default`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_U_Microsoft_Outlook_Cached_Mode_Default.en.md) | Alternative to the Managed variant, for an organisation that does want shared mailboxes cached. | [`WIN - D - Defender Update Ring 1 Pilot`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Defender_Update_Ring_1_Pilot.en.md) | **SEC-Update-Ring1** — Pilot group for Defender updates. | A.8.7, A.8.8, A.8.32 |
| [`WIN - D - Defender Update Ring 2 UAT`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Defender_Update_Ring_2_UAT.en.md) | **SEC-Update-Ring2** — UAT group for Defender updates. | A.8.7, A.8.8, A.8.32 |
| [`WIN - D - Windows Hello for Business Multi User`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Windows_Hello_for_Business_Multi_User.en.md) | **SEC-Shared-Devices** — Shared devices. The only one you can assign alongside its counterpart: the four overlapping settings are set to the same value. | A.5.17, A.8.5 |
| [`WIN - D - Windows Update Ring 1 Pilot`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/DeviceConfigurations/Baseline_WIN_D_Windows_Update_Ring_1_Pilot.en.md) | **SEC-Update-Ring1** — Pilot group for Windows updates. | A.8.8, A.8.32 |
| [`WIN - D - Windows Update Ring 2 UAT`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/DeviceConfigurations/Baseline_WIN_D_Windows_Update_Ring_2_UAT.en.md) | **SEC-Update-Ring2** — UAT group for Windows updates. | A.8.8, A.8.32 |
| [`WIN - D - Wireless Shared Devices`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Wireless_Shared_Devices.en.md) | **SEC-Shared-Devices** — Shared devices. On a single-user laptop this makes working from home and in hotels impossible. | A.8.1, A.8.20 |

| [`AND - U - Compliance Defender for Endpoint`](../IntuneTemplate/AND/CompliancePolicies/Baseline_AND_U_Compliance_Defender_for_Endpoint.en.md) | Awaiting three prerequisites: a Defender for Endpoint licence, the Defender–Intune connector with Android enabled, and the Defender app deployed via Managed Google Play. Without those three, every device becomes non-compliant. | A.8.7, A.8.16 |

| [`IOS - D - Enterprise SSO`](../IntuneTemplate/IOS/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_IOS_D_Enterprise_SSO.en.md) | Awaiting the first iOS enrolment and Microsoft Authenticator on the device: Apple only accepts the SSO extension via MDM, and without Authenticator there is no plug-in that runs it. | A.5.17, A.8.5 |
| [`IOS - D - Passcode`](../IntuneTemplate/IOS/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_IOS_D_Passcode.en.md) | Awaiting the first iOS enrolment. Watch out during the first deployment: a user with a four-digit or simple passcode must change it at the next unlock. | A.5.17, A.8.1, A.8.5 |

| [`IOS - U - Compliance Password`](../IntuneTemplate/IOS/CompliancePolicies/Baseline_IOS_U_Compliance_Password.en.md) | Awaiting the first iOS enrolment. | A.5.17, A.8.1, A.8.5 |
| [`MAC - D - Azure Files Cloud Kerberos`](../IntuneTemplate/MAC/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_MAC_D_Azure_Files_Cloud_Kerberos.en.md) | Waits until there is a storage account with Entra Kerberos as identity source. An account that is already on Microsoft Entra Domain Services or AD DS cannot have that at the same time, and switching it affects everything already running on that account. On a Mac with a valid cloud TGT, such an account yields AADSTS700016 — the KDC knows no application for that file service. The profile itself is finished and account-independent: `Hosts` is set to `.windows.net` and thus covers every storage account. As soon as there is one with Entra Kerberos this can move to phase 1, with as second prerequisite that Microsoft enables the tenant for the macOS preview (azurefiles@microsoft.com). | A.8.5 |

| [`MAC - D - Wifi Guest`](../IntuneTemplate/MAC/DeviceConfigurations/Baseline_MAC_D_Wifi_Guest.en.md) | SSID and PSK are set to a placeholder. Assigning before they are filled in produces a profile that connects nowhere. Set the phase to 1 once the real values are in, and not earlier than Wifi Corporate. | A.8.20, A.8.21 |
| [`WIN - D - Wifi Corporate`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/DeviceConfigurations/Baseline_WIN_D_Wifi_Corporate.en.md) | SSID and PSK are set to a placeholder. Assigning before they are filled in produces a profile that connects nowhere. Set the phase to 1 once the real values are in. | A.8.1, A.8.20, A.8.21 |
| [`WIN - D - Wifi Guest`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/DeviceConfigurations/Baseline_WIN_D_Wifi_Guest.en.md) | SSID and PSK are set to a placeholder. Assigning before they are filled in produces a profile that connects nowhere. Set the phase to 1 once the real values are in, and not earlier than Wifi Corporate. | A.8.20, A.8.21 |
| [`WIN - D - Windows AI Recall Boundaries`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Windows_AI_Recall_Boundaries.en.md) | Belongs with [Baseline] - WIN - D - Windows AI Permitted and does nothing without that policy: if Recall is off, there is nothing to restrict. | [`WIN - D - Windows Event Forwarding`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Windows_Event_Forwarding.en.md) | Does nothing without a Windows Event Collector with source-initiated subscriptions that is reachable from the devices (VPN, Always On VPN or internal network). Anyone who centralises logs via Defender for Endpoint, Microsoft Sentinel or the Azure Monitor Agent does not need this policy. | A.8.15, A.8.16 |
| [`WIN - U - Compliance Defender for Endpoint Risk`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/CompliancePolicies/Baseline_WIN_U_Compliance_Defender_for_Endpoint_Risk.en.md) | Awaiting the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint connector in Intune (Endpoint security → Microsoft Defender for Endpoint → 'Connect Windows devices … to Defender for Endpoint' on) and a Defender for Endpoint P1/P2 or Business licence. Without the connector, every device reports 'not compliant' or 'not available' on this check. | A.5.15, A.8.7, A.8.16 |

### D. Pilot — phase 2 (42)

Noticeable to users or may break something. Decision: accept the consequences after the pilot and move to phase 1.
Until that decision, the control the policy implements is not covered.

| Policy | Consequence to be accepted | Standards (ISO) |
|---|---|---|
| [`AND - U - Corporate AI Restricted`](../IntuneTemplate/AND/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_AND_U_Corporate_AI_Restricted.en.md) | Users lose Circle to Search and Gemini's screen context on the work profile or the whole device. Whether that fits is an organisational decision about generative AI, as with Windows AI Restricted; pilot group first, and do not assign for an organisation that allows these assistants. | A.5.10, A.5.34, A.8.12 |
| [`AND - U - Corporate Data Protection`](../IntuneTemplate/AND/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_AND_U_Corporate_Data_Protection.en.md) | Users notice it immediately: no screenshots, no files via Bluetooth, and a fully managed device can no longer be reset by the user — IT has to wipe it. Pilot group first; without fully managed or corporate-owned work profile enrolment it does nothing. | A.7.9, A.8.1, A.8.12 |
| [`MAC - D - Apple Intelligence Restricted`](../IntuneTemplate/MAC/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_MAC_D_Apple_Intelligence_Restricted.en.md) | Users see Writing Tools, summaries, Genmoji, Image Playground and the ChatGPT integration disappear. That is intended, but it is visible and deserves an announcement. Choose per organisation between this one and the Permitted variant — never assign both. | A.5.10, A.5.34, A.8.12 |
| [`MAC - D - FileVault`](../IntuneTemplate/MAC/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_MAC_D_FileVault.en.md) | Encrypts the disk and asks the user to cooperate. Check in the pilot that the recovery key actually appears in Intune before you deploy broadly. | A.7.9, A.8.1, A.8.24 |
| [`MAC - D - Login Window`](../IntuneTemplate/MAC/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_MAC_D_Login_Window.en.md) | At the login window, users must type their account name instead of clicking their name. Announce it. After a restart the user still sees the account list of the FileVault unlock screen; this setting applies to the login window after that (sign out, switch users). | A.5.10, A.8.5 |
| [`MAC - D - Passcode and Screen Lock`](../IntuneTemplate/MAC/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_MAC_D_Passcode_and_Screen_Lock.en.md) | Users with a shorter or simpler password must change it at their next sign-in. | A.5.17, A.7.7, A.8.1, A.8.5 |
| [`MAC - D - Recovery Lock`](../IntuneTemplate/MAC/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_MAC_D_Recovery_Lock.en.md) | Anyone who needs recoveryOS — reinstalling macOS, Disk Utility from recovery, another startup disk — must from now on request the password from the service desk. Check in the pilot that the password is visible in Intune before you deploy broadly. | A.5.17, A.7.9, A.8.1, A.8.18 |
| [`MAC - D - Restrictions Hardening`](../IntuneTemplate/MAC/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_MAC_D_Restrictions_Hardening.en.md) | Starting an unsigned app via right-click → Open is no longer possible, and a user can no longer install a profile or certificate by hand (for example from a VPN vendor, a test environment or a Wi-Fi portal). Inventory in the pilot who does that now; those installations should go through Intune from now on. | A.5.34, A.8.9, A.8.19 |
| [`MAC - D - Screensaver`](../IntuneTemplate/MAC/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_MAC_D_Screensaver.en.md) | Anyone used to getting the screen back without a password within a minute of the screen saver must now use their password or Touch ID straight away. Noticeable, not breaking; pilot and announce first. | A.7.7, A.8.1, A.8.5 |
| [`MAC - D - Software Updates`](../IntuneTemplate/MAC/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_MAC_D_Software_Updates.en.md) | Updates are installed automatically and enforced no later than 30 days after release with a restart at 12:30 — including for a new major version of macOS. Check in the pilot how the restart time falls and whether business apps can handle the new major version. Beta enrolment is no longer possible. | A.8.8, A.8.19 |
| [`MAC - U - Compliance OS Version`](../IntuneTemplate/MAC/CompliancePolicies/Baseline_MAC_U_Compliance_OS_Version.en.md) | A Mac below macOS 14 becomes non-compliant and loses access via Conditional Access. OVERZICHT.md already mentions that older Macs do not get the update profile; this policy makes that visible instead of silent. First check how many Macs it affects. Grace period is 72 hours. | A.8.8, A.8.19 |
| [`WIN - D - Access Control`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Access_Control.en.md) | Users must type their full name instead of clicking it, and they see a banner. First adjust the banner text to your own organisation's name. | A.5.15, A.5.17, A.8.5 |
| [`WIN - D - Account Lockout`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Account_Lockout.en.md) | The machine threshold puts a device into BitLocker recovery after ten failed attempts. That is recoverable (the key is stored in Entra ID) but generates a helpdesk ticket; check in the pilot how often it happens. | A.5.15, A.5.17, A.8.5 |
| [`WIN - D - Administrator Protection`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Administrator_Protection.en.md) | Changes how an administrator works: no more permanently elevated rights, but a confirmation per action. Scripts and tools that silently rely on administrator rights will notice. Windows 11 24H2 and later; on older builds it does nothing. | A.8.2 |
| [`WIN - D - Bluetooth Allowed Services`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Bluetooth_Allowed_Services.en.md) | An allowlist turns off everything that is not on it, and which Bluetooth devices are in use you only know once you look. In the pilot, test at least a mouse, a keyboard, a headset (classic and LE Audio), calling via Phone Link with an iPhone and an Android phone, and a passkey sign-in with the QR code. Only takes effect after a restart. | A.8.12, A.8.20 |
| [`WIN - D - Cryptography`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Cryptography.en.md) | An internal system that only speaks TLS 1.0/1.1 becomes unreachable. That is intended, but it has to be known. | A.8.24 |
| [`WIN - D - Device Guard and Credential Guard`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Device_Guard_and_Credential_Guard.en.md) | Requires a restart, and memory integrity (HVCI) does not load drivers that were not built for it — think of old VPN, printer and dock drivers. Check in the pilot that everything still starts. | A.5.17, A.8.1, A.8.7 |
| [`WIN - D - Disable NTLM`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Disable_NTLM.en.md) | Refuses all NTLM, inbound and outbound. Whatever cannot use Kerberos breaks: applications that connect by IP address, devices outside the domain, and shares for which the device gets no Kerberos ticket — an Entra-joined device opening a share on Entra Domain Services falls back to NTLM. Before the pilot, read Microsoft-Windows-NTLM/Operational on a few Windows 11 24H2 devices (4020/4021 outbound, 4022/4023 inbound): that logging is enabled there by default and shows what would break. | A.8.5 |
| [`WIN - D - Enrollment Hardening`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Enrollment_Hardening.en.md) | Affects the initial setup of a device, not a running device. Test on one Autopilot device: without a network the user cannot proceed, and that is intended — but it must match how devices are deployed in your organisation. | A.5.9, A.5.15, A.8.1 |
| [`WIN - D - Google Chrome Extensions`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Google_Chrome_Extensions.en.md) | ExtensionInstallBlocklist '*' also disables extensions that are already installed, so every Chrome user loses their extensions. First check which ones are in use (Defender Vulnerability Management → Browser extensions) and put what is needed on ExtensionInstallAllowlist in a tenant-specific copy. | A.8.19 |
| [`WIN - D - Google Chrome Security`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Google_Chrome_Security.en.md) | Noticeable for Chrome users: browser sign-in, sync and saving new passwords are turned off. Remote debugging is turned off too, which breaks automated tests (Puppeteer, Playwright, Selenium) against the installed Chrome. Pilot group first. | A.8.7, A.8.12, A.8.23, A.8.24 |
| [`WIN - D - In-Box App Removal`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_In_Box_App_Removal.en.md) | Removes built-in apps, including from devices already in use. Check in the pilot whether anyone misses one. | A.8.19 |
| [`WIN - D - Kernel DMA Protection`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Kernel_DMA_Protection.en.md) | A dock or eGPU without DMA remapping no longer works. Test with the docks present in the fleet. | A.7.9, A.8.1 |
| [`WIN - D - Logon Hardening`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Logon_Hardening.en.md) | Users will now have to press CTRL+ALT+DEL before the sign-in screen. Communicate this before the broad deployment. | A.5.15, A.8.5, A.8.20 |
| [`WIN - D - Microsoft Edge DNS over HTTPS Automatic`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Microsoft_Edge_DNS_over_HTTPS_Automatic.en.md) | Automatic is the Edge default, but once enforced the user can no longer turn it off or choose their own resolver. Test on the pilot group whether internal names and any web proxy/DNS filter keep working. | A.8.20, A.8.24 |
| [`WIN - D - Network Authentication Hardening`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Network_Authentication_Hardening.en.md) | Closing PKU2U breaks Remote Desktop to another Entra-joined device with Entra credentials via the old sign-in method, and P-node breaks NetBIOS name resolution via broadcast in a network without DNS or WINS. Pilot group first. | A.8.5, A.8.20 |
| [`WIN - D - Printing Hardening`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Printing_Hardening.en.md) | Windows Protected Print drops printers that have no Mopria driver. Inventory the printer fleet first. | A.8.7, A.8.19, A.8.20 |
| [`WIN - D - Remote Access Hardening`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Remote_Access_Hardening.en.md) | Check that no management script or monitoring tool relies on winrs. Enter-PSSession and Invoke-Command keep working, winrs does not. | A.5.15, A.8.20, A.8.21 |
| [`WIN - D - Removable Storage`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Removable_Storage.en.md) | Writing to USB sticks, external drives and phones is blocked, and a user notices that immediately. Note: until this policy is broadly deployed, removable storage is not restricted anywhere — BitLocker deliberately leaves removabledrivesrequireencryption off, because this block covers it. | A.7.10, A.8.12 |
| [`WIN - D - Script File Associations`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Script_File_Associations.en.md) | Double-clicking a .js, .vbs or .hta file will now open Notepad. A logon or installation script started that way will then do nothing; check in the pilot whether such scripts are in circulation. | A.8.7 |
| [`WIN - D - Security Log Monitoring`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Security_Log_Monitoring.en.md) | Module logging for all modules (*) produces a lot of event 4103 in Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational. First check on the pilot group what that does to log volume and any SIEM ingest; see IntuneTemplate/WIN/Remediations/event-log-sizes for the log size. | A.8.15, A.8.16 |
| [`WIN - D - Windows AI Features Restricted`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Windows_AI_Features_Restricted.en.md) | Users see the AI buttons in Paint disappear. That is intended, but it is visible and deserves an announcement. Choose per organisation between this one and the Permitted variant — never assign both. | A.5.10, A.5.34, A.8.1 |
| [`WIN - D - Windows Component Hardening`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Windows_Component_Hardening.en.md) | Noticeable in two places: 'Continue on this device' (Continue experiences) disappears, and a kiosk device that uses AutoAdminLogon no longer signs in automatically. Pilot group first; keep kiosks out of this policy. | A.8.1, A.8.9 |
| [`WIN - D - Windows Hello for Business`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Windows_Hello_for_Business.en.md) | Every user is guided through PIN setup at their next sign-in, and a device without a TPM does not get WHfB. Goes into the pilot together with WIN - U - Windows Hello for Business: one in the pilot and the other on everyone makes the pilot pointless. | A.5.17, A.8.5 |
| [`WIN - D - Windows Hello Passkey PIN Complexity Alphanumeric`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_D_Windows_Hello_Passkey_PIN_Complexity_Alphanumeric.en.md) | Goes into the pilot together with WIN - D - Windows Hello for Business and WIN - U - Windows Hello for Business — they are in the same phase and await this same decision. Assigning complexity to users without WHfB set up does nothing; conversely, a user with WHfB but without this policy falls back to six digits. Watch the number of PIN resets in the pilot: that is the cost of this variant. There are four PIN complexity policies and only one may ever be assigned: `WIN - D - Windows Hello Passkey PIN Complexity Alphanumeric` / `Numeric` (the passkey-named set) and `WIN - D - Windows Hello PIN Complexity Alphanumeric` / `Numeric` (the generic, older one). Two assigned policies that set the same setting to a different value produce a Conflict in Intune, after which neither is applied. | A.5.17, A.8.5 |
| [`WIN - U - AI Usage Control Restricted`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_U_AI_Usage_Control_Restricted.en.md) | Takes over the Edge URL block list from Microsoft Edge User Experience — that setting has already been removed there. Check in the pilot that no legitimate site is blocked. Choose per organisation between this one and the Permitted variant; never assign both. | A.5.10, A.5.19, A.8.1, A.8.23 |
| [`WIN - U - Compliance OS Version`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/CompliancePolicies/Baseline_WIN_U_Compliance_OS_Version.en.md) | A device below the minimum becomes non-compliant and thereby loses access via Conditional Access. First check in the reporting how many devices this affects — the answer should be zero, but you must have seen that rather than assumed it. Grace period is 72 hours. | A.8.8, A.8.19 |
| [`WIN - U - File Sharing Restrictions`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_U_File_Sharing_Restrictions.en.md) | A user who is used to sharing a folder from their profile via File Explorer will see that option disappear. Sharing via OneDrive and Teams keeps working. | A.8.3, A.8.12 |
| [`WIN - U - Microsoft Edge Management`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_U_Microsoft_Edge_Management.en.md) | Reverses precedence: policy from the Edge Management Service then wins over the Edge policy from this baseline. Anyone with the Edge Administrator role can therefore override settings from Microsoft Edge Security and User Experience. First record who has that role before this is broadly deployed. | A.8.9 |
| [`WIN - U - Microsoft Outlook Cached Mode Managed`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_U_Microsoft_Outlook_Cached_Mode_Managed.en.md) | Affects every existing profile: Outlook rebuilds the OST and a shared mailbox in the profile goes from cached to online. That is visible — the first synchronisation takes time and bandwidth, and anyone used to working offline in a shared mailbox notices it immediately. Pilot group first, and check there how many profiles have a shared mailbox. | A.8.9 |
| [`WIN - U - Microsoft Teams`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_U_Microsoft_Teams.en.md) | Blocks signing in with an account from another tenant. That is intended, but anyone using a second work account in Teams notices it immediately — check in the pilot whether that occurs. | A.5.14, A.5.15, A.8.12 |
| [`WIN - U - Windows Hello for Business`](../IntuneTemplate/WIN/SettingsCatalog/Baseline_WIN_U_Windows_Hello_for_Business.en.md) | Belongs with WIN - D - Windows Hello for Business and goes into the pilot together with it — on all users it would still set up WHfB on every device, and then the pilot tests nothing. | A.5.17, A.8.5 |

## What a licence would add

The starting point is **Microsoft 365 Business Premium** (maximum 300 users). What it includes:

- Microsoft Entra ID P1
- Microsoft Intune Plan 1
- Microsoft Defender for Business (Windows, Mac, Android, iOS)
- Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 1
- Windows 11 Business (Pro level, not Enterprise)
- Purview Information Protection and DLP

Below, per licence, which policies from this baseline start working because of it, and which
standards that touches. Policies waiting on a pilot, an organisational decision or an enrolment are
**not** listed here — they have their own reason in [Organisational decisions](#organisational-decisions-and-residual-risks).

### Microsoft Entra ID P2

*standalone per user, or as part of the Defender Suite for Business Premium*

Risk-based Conditional Access is listed as 'P1: No' in Microsoft's own licensing table. Four templates in the CA repo use userRiskLevels or signInRiskLevels as a condition; on P1 those conditions never become true, so the policies do nothing — while they do deploy and count as present in the assessment.

| Side | Policies |
|---|---|
| Conditional Access (4) | `CXNM - STANDARD - 1090 - BLOCK - HighRisk SignIns`, `CXNM - STANDARD - 1100 - BLOCK - HighRisk Users`, `CXNM - STANDARD - 2010 - GRANT - MediumRisk Signins`, `CXNM - STANDARD - 2020 - GRANT - MediumRisk Users` |

**No new policy, but coverage:** Privileged Identity Management: roles just-in-time instead of permanent, with approval and an audit trail. A.5.3 is now explicitly listed in COMPLIANCE.md as 'Set up Entra/Intune RBAC and PIM — outside this baseline'.

ISO: `A.5.3 Functiescheiding`, `A.8.2 Speciale toegangsrechten` · NIS2: `(i)`

### Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps

*standalone, or as part of the Defender Suite for Business Premium*

CA policy 3060 routes browser sessions through MDCA as a session control. Without that licence, the session control cannot be selected in the policy.

| Side | Policies |
|---|---|
| Conditional Access (1) | `CXNM - STANDARD - 3060 - SESSION - Defender for Cloud Apps` |

### Microsoft Defender Suite for Business Premium

*add-on to Business Premium, commercial and non-profit*

Bundles entra-id-p2 and defender-cloud-apps, so the same five policies. What comes on top is not a policy but investigation capacity: threat hunting, live response, six months of retention and automated investigation & response.

**No new policy, but coverage:** Automated investigation & response does the assessment and containment; six months of device retention and advanced hunting provide the evidence that A.5.28 requires and that substantiates a NIS2 notification within 24 hours.

ISO: `A.5.7 Informatie en analyses over dreigingen`, `A.5.25 Beoordelen van en besluiten over informatiebeveiligingsgebeurtenissen`, `A.5.26 Reageren op informatiebeveiligingsincidenten`, `A.5.28 Verzamelen van bewijsmateriaal` · NIS2: `(b)`

> **Note.** Defender for Business and Defender for Endpoint Plan 2 CANNOT coexist in one tenant. Microsoft: an organisation with both 'defaults to the Defender for Business experience'. To actually get P2 you must license every user and ask Microsoft Support to convert the tenant. Buying it halfway therefore gets you the price of P2 with the capabilities of Defender for Business.

### Windows 11 Enterprise E3 of E5

*separate licence alongside Business Premium; availability differs per channel — check with the distributor*

Personal Data Encryption and Credential Guard are listed as 'Windows Pro: No' in Microsoft's edition table. Business Premium provides Windows 11 Business, which is Pro level.

| Side | Policies |
|---|---|
| Intune (1) | `WIN - U - Personal Data Encryption` |

**Partially: WIN - D - Device Guard and Credential Guard.** One of the eight settings (deviceguard_lsacfgflags, Credential Guard) is Enterprise-only. The other seven — VBS, HVCI, System Guard Secure Launch, LSA protection, Secure Boot with DMA — work on Pro. This policy is therefore meaningful without this licence; it contains one inert setting.

**Trade-off.** On a fleet with BitLocker on all devices and OneDrive Known Folder Move, the marginal gain of PDE is small: the disk is already encrypted and the folders are already in the cloud. PDE protects against a different scenario — a powered-on, unlocked device on which another user signs in. Buy this if a contract or statement of applicability requires it, not because it sounds complete.

### Microsoft Entra Workload ID Premium

*separate licence; NOT included in Entra ID P2 nor in the Defender Suite*

Risk detection on workload identities is a separate SKU. This is the pitfall with the Defender Suite: P2 covers user risk, not workload risk.

| Side | Policies |
|---|---|
| Conditional Access (1) | `CXNM - STANDARD - 1140 - BLOCK - Managed Identities At Risk` |

### Microsoft Entra Agent ID

*not yet available in every tenant*

The five agent templates require agent identities. This is not a purchasing decision but an availability issue; they are therefore set to report-only until the capability is available.

| Side | Policies |
|---|---|
| Conditional Access (5) | `CXNM - STANDARD - 1150 - BLOCK - Risky Agent Identities`, `CXNM - STANDARD - 1160 - BLOCK - Agent Identities To Agent Resources`, `CXNM - STANDARD - 1170 - BLOCK - Risky Agent Users`, `CXNM - STANDARD - 1180 - BLOCK - Agent Users Outside Compliant Network`, `CXNM - STANDARD - 2160 - GRANT - Agent Users Compliant Device` |

### What you do not need to pay for

Things that are easily assumed to require a licence, but that Business Premium
already covers. They are listed here so that nobody pays for them by accident.
The six Defender compliance policies in phases 3 and 4 are waiting for CONFIGURATION, not money:
the Defender–Intune connector, and the Defender app deployed via Managed Google Play or VPP.
Defender for Business covers Windows, Mac, Android and iOS.

| What | Why it already works |
|---|---|
| Attack Surface Reduction rules | Microsoft: 'ASR rules are a Microsoft Defender Antivirus feature available on any edition of Windows.' Only centralised reporting requires more; the rules themselves enforce on Pro. |
| Defender on Android and iOS | Defender for Business supports Windows, Mac, Android and iOS/iPadOS. The associated compliance policies are waiting for the connector and the app deployment, not for a licence. |
| Conditional Access itself | Entra ID P1 is included in Business Premium. Only the four risk-based policies require P2. |
| VBS, HVCI, LSA protection | Work on Windows Pro. Only Credential Guard within that same policy requires Enterprise. |
